gaps.quote: Each role stream then holds $V/(2W)$ bits (cited).
gaps.note: Wrong constant. Rows are dealt cyclically to W roles and V counts all stored bits, so each role stream holds V/W bits, not V/(2W). The paper (line 127-128) says: 'All role streams have the same local address set and each contains $V/W$ bits.' Also the factor 2 is never explained.

gaps.quote: Frames therefore pass through every gate, linear or not.
gaps.note: Overstated and contradicts the preceding derivation, which uses linearity of the frame and fixed scalar coefficients of a pointwise linear gate. The common frame commutes only with pointwise linear gates (paper line 137: 'At a pointwise linear gate G, the common frame commutes with the gate'; line 812 uses R-linearity). For a nonlinear gate the identity fails.

gaps.quote: its operator is $D_\nu$, however many gates it passes through.
gaps.note: The page just said the route applies eps_w D_sink D_source^{-1}. With source frame I and sink frame D_nu the operator is eps_w D_nu, equal to D_nu only when the sign is +1 (as for scratch roles). The paper (line 144-146) gives the scalar sign together with the endpoint operator.

gaps.term: source and sink nodes, gates, edges
gaps.quote: Each source, gate and sink $\nu$ carries an invertible linear operator
gaps.note: The page never says what the nodes of the network are: that each wire starts at a source, passes through gates in time order, and ends at a sink, with edges between consecutive nodes, nor that the gates are fixed linear maps on several wires. The reader cannot tell what a route, source(w) or sink(w) is, or why a gate has one frame for all its wires.
